frequency_question: How often do structural frictions and institutional veto points prevent the successful signing of a bilateral water treaty successor within a compressed deadline?
membership_rule: Includes formal negotiations for renewing or replacing major transboundary water sharing treaties where an existing treaty is expiring or has expired. Excludes greenfield treaties with no prior framework.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty Permanent Commission modifications/discussions
Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase II supplemental agreements
Nile Basin Cooperative Framework Agreement final push
Colorado River Basin Minute 323 (US-Mexico successor to Minute 319)

coverage_note: 6 named cases representing major transboundary water treaty renewals under friction constraints since 1990.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller basin agreements handled purely at administrative rather than bilateral treaty levels.
skeleton: 6 historical negotiation instances of transboundary water renewals under structural friction and deadlines; 3 achieved formal signed successor texts.
validity_reason: Global transboundary water negotiation dynamics and institutional friction patterns evolve slowly over decades.
